summary: Colombia admits passport holders of about 100 countries — including the US, UK, EU, Canada and most of the Americas — visa-free for 90 days, extendable in-country to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. Nationalities that do need a visa apply online for a Visitor (V) visa through the Foreign Ministry, and every traveler must submit the free Check-Mig form before both entering and leaving by air.

conditionalWaivers.text: Citizens of China, India and Vietnam (plus a few other listed nationalities) holding a US or Schengen visa valid for more than 6 months — or permanent residence there — may enter Colombia visa-free for up to 90 days.

source.name: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Colombia

fee.notes: USD 54 application (study) fee, plus an issuance fee of about USD 82 for most nationalities if approved; amounts vary by nationality and are updated by resolution. Check the Cancillería fee table before applying.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months from your date of entry into Colombia.

source.name: UK FCDO — Colombia travel advice (entry requirements)

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Yellow fever vaccination is strongly recommended for most of Colombia below 2,300 m and is REQUIRED for entry to several national parks — including the Amazon region and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Tayrona area) — where the certificate is checked. Some arrivals from risk countries may also be asked for it.

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry requirement, but strongly recommended — private clinics expect payment or proof of insurance, and medical evacuation from remote areas is costly.

onwardTicket.text: Visa-free visitors must hold a return or onward ticket — airlines routinely check it before boarding flights to Colombia.

source.name: UK FCDO — Colombia travel advice (entry requirements)

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is set, but immigration officers may ask you to show means to cover your stay.

declarations.name: Check-Mig form
declarations.submitWindow: Between 72 hours and 1 hour before your flight
declarations.text: Everyone flying into AND out of Colombia must complete the free Check-Mig form on the Migración Colombia website or app, between 72 hours and 1 hour before the flight. It is completely free — beware of lookalike sites that charge for it.

currencyLimits.text: Cash or monetary instruments of USD 10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure — undeclared excess amounts can be seized.

notes: Exporting pre-Columbian artefacts, coca leaf products and wildlife is illegal and heavily penalized.
Personal duty-free allowance is generally up to USD 1,500 of goods in addition to personal effects.

payments.text: Cards are widely accepted in city restaurants, hotels and malls, but cash rules in markets, small towns, taxis and rural areas. Carry small COP notes; ATMs are plentiful in cities. Use ones inside banks or malls.

safety.text: Most tourist areas — Bogotá, Medellín, Cartagena, the Coffee Axis — are fine with sensible precautions, but robbery and drink-spiking scams do target tourists, and some border and rural regions remain no-go areas. Avoid displaying valuables, use app-based taxis and check regional advice before traveling off the beaten path.

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to March is the main dry season across most of the country; July and August bring a second drier window. Being equatorial, Colombia varies more by altitude than by season.

tips.text: Check-Mig is FREE at migracioncolombia.gov.co and required for both your inbound and outbound flights. Third-party sites charging a fee for it are scams — never pay.

Do not hail taxis on the street at night. Use app-based services (Uber, DiDi, Cabify) or hotel-arranged cars. Keep phones out of sight on the street and be wary of overly friendly strangers offering food or drinks.

Bogotá sits at 2,640 m. Take it easy on arrival, hydrate, and go light on alcohol for the first day or two. Tap water is safe in Bogotá and Medellín; stick to bottled water on the coast and in rural areas.

Carry your yellow fever certificate if you plan to visit Tayrona, the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta or the Amazon — vaccination is checked for park entry and must be done at least 10 days before travel.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days, extendable in-country to a maximum of 180 days per calendar year. They must complete the free Check-Mig form before their inbound and outbound flights and hold an onward ticket.

faq.question: What is Check-Mig and is it really free?
faq.answer: Check-Mig is Migración Colombia's mandatory online immigration form, submitted between 72 hours and 1 hour before every international flight into or out of Colombia. It is completely free at migracioncolombia.gov.co — any site charging for it is a scam.

faq.question: How can I stay in Colombia longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: Before your first 90 days expire, apply to Migración Colombia (online or at an office) for a Permiso Temporal de Permanencia extension of up to 90 more days. The hard cap for visa-free visitors is 180 days per calendar year — beyond that you need a visa.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Colombia?
faq.answer: It is not required for regular entry from most countries, but it is strongly recommended for lowland regions and REQUIRED to enter several national parks, including Tayrona and the Amazon. Get vaccinated at least 10 days before travel and carry the ICVP certificate.

faq.question: Do Indian or Chinese citizens need a visa for Colombia?
faq.answer: Generally yes — a Visitor (V) visa applied for online through the Cancillería. However, holders of a valid US or Schengen visa or residence permit can enter visa-free for up to 90 days, and Colombia announced a visa waiver for Chinese tourists in 2025. Confirm the current status with a Colombian consulate before booking.
